deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 34% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.2% = 10-year Treasury 5.2% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (3%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 15% last year; 13%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 12% (3 years ago 12%, about the same) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $12 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 22% (3 years ago 11%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $28.2B, up 12% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 61% vs quarterly sales up 12% (days to collect 31 → 44). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 13%/yr over 3 years and 12%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 13% vs a 5-year range of 2–13% (median 9%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price. Swing: no trade while the price is stuck between support and resistance.
summary.act_at: Wait. Consider buying at 251.93 only if cash flow improves; fuller value is at 238.65.

note.happening: Amazon closed at 257.75, down 3.34% on the day. That puts it just above its main support zone of 251.93–257.04 and just below resistance at 258.08–261.12. The biggest reported news is a Vulcan rocket failure that destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites (speculative). Zoox robotaxis are also now available on Uber in Las Vegas. No earnings date is in the data.
note.business: Three things in the latest filing (2026-10-30) affect the business itself. First, sales growth is slowing. Quarterly revenue rose 12.09% from a year earlier, compared with 16.61% two quarters ago. Second, profitability is improving. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 13.09% from 11.02%. Third, cash is going the wrong way. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, is -46.9B over 12 months, against +10.6B a year earlier. Debt exceeds cash by 66.7B, though liquidity of 114.2B leaves no near-term funding strain. The filings also flag that unpaid customer bills are up 61% while sales are up 12%, which can mean sales were pulled forward. The reported satellite loss hurts the Leo internet project and its timeline, but not Amazon's core demand. The Zoox, Instagram affiliate-link and James Bond reports affect sentiment and long-term options, not this year's numbers. Most at risk: cash flow, and whether today's peak margin holds. Not at risk: overall scale, with revenue of 797.5B over 12 months.

worth.text: No discounted-cash-flow value is available because free cash flow is negative. Value rests on Amazon's own price-to-sales history (price compared with yearly sales per share). That method gives 187.93 at the low end, 238.65 in the middle and 266.4 at the top. At 257.75, the price sits in the upper part of that range. Price-to-sales of 3.5 is at the 82nd percentile of Amazon's own 5-year history. The filing risks note that the price needs about 34% a year growth, against 13% a year delivered over 3 years. Against peers, Amazon looks cheap: their median price-to-sales is 6.8, and the growth-adjusted ratio versus peers is 0.6. The gap between the two methods comes down to one question: is Amazon valued like its own history or like its peers? Earnings multiples point the same cautious way. The price is 20.9 times trailing earnings but 24.2 times next year's, because analysts expect next-year EPS (10.67) to be below this year's (12.8). Note that the valuation summary in DATA quotes a stale price of 266.66.
worth.key_assumption: Amazon's price-to-sales stays within its own 5-year range and does not move toward the peer median of 6.8.

bull: Operating margin rose to 13.09% from 11.02%, so each dollar of sales now earns more.
Price-to-sales of 3.5 is about half the peer median of 6.8, with growth-adjusted EV/sales at 0.6 of peers.
Next-year EPS estimates rose 1.4% over 30 days, and revenue grew to 797.5B from 691.3B over 12 months.
bear: Free cash flow fell to -46.9B from +10.6B a year earlier, and debt exceeds cash by 66.7B.
Quarterly sales growth slowed to 12.09% from 16.61% two quarters ago, while unpaid customer bills rose 61%.
Next-quarter EPS estimates were cut 2.6% in 30 days, and next-year EPS of 10.67 is below this year's 12.8.

levels.what: Bottom of the strongest support zone (6 touches). A first entry only if free cash flow stops getting worse.
Bottom of the deeper support zone (9 touches), near the 200-day average of 244.69. A close below it breaks the range.

longterm.why: Better margins do not yet outweigh slowing growth and cash burn at a price in the upper part of the value range. The business grade is D and the committee call is 'Reduce'.

swing.why: The price sits in a narrow gap between support at 251.93–257.04 and resistance at 258.08–261.12, so the upside to resistance is small for a sensible stop. Recent swings (realized volatility 40.1) are also bigger than options price in (implied volatility 33.2).

decision.timing: No earnings date is in the data. Options to 2026-11-20 price a move of about 3.9%, so the next point to reassess is a test of 251.93 or a close above 261.12.

change_mind: A filing showing 12-month free cash flow back above zero (from -46.9B) while the price holds 251.93 would turn 'wait' into 'buy'.
A close below 244.3, the bottom of the deeper support zone, would shift the stance toward 'avoid' until the price nears 238.65.
A close above 267.56, the top of resistance, would break the range, but it would also put the price above the 266.4 value top. That would not by itself justify buying.
note.what_changed: Unchanged: still 'wait', because the 3.34% drop to 257.75 leaves the price above the 238.65 value midpoint while free cash flow stays at -46.9B.
